display.title: Episode 31: The Forbidden Road, Chapter 2 (Shiva Asar B'Tammuz)
display.summary_short: Reb Beryl promises his Rebbe to give a tenth of his wealth to tzedakah, and a drunken officer loses the paper that took his fortune. Plus listeners' riddles and the five sad events of 17 Tammuz.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi thanks listeners for their summer letters and offers tapes of all thirty programs aired so far, then leads the Hakochainik march. After a recap, a ten-year-old girl from a Boro Park school recites the Shema. The story concludes: the Rebbe tells the penniless Reb Beryl that it is never too late for teshuvah, explains that Hashem gives wealth so that one can give tzedakah, and asks him to promise a tenth of all his money to charity. As Reb Beryl and his wife say Tehillim, the officer who holds the signed paper celebrates with wine, falls asleep drunk, and loses the crumpled paper; afraid of punishment, he never reports it. Reb Beryl asks the melamed's forgiveness, brings him back to teach his son, and gives generously, learning that tzedakah is the true path to wealth. After a sponsor message, two listeners' letters are read, one with riddles. Uncle Yossi closes with the five sad events of the 17th of Tammuz, which falls that Thursday, and a prayer for Moshiach.
display.lesson: Wealth is given so that we can give tzedakah; the more we give, the more Hashem blesses us. It is never too late for teshuvah.
